item.title: Gambit 1.0
item.description:
# Gambit 1.0
Released November 5, 2026.
Gambit's first stable release. The browser is now its own thing rather than a fork wearing someone else's name: every surface says Gambit, the agent panel looks like the rest of the app, and updates come from Gambit's own feed.
## The agent, rebuilt
- **A panel that matches the app.** The agent pane was the last piece still drawn in the old fork's palette — a burnt orange that belonged to another product, and an empty state that was a sparkle in a gradient circle. It now uses Gambit's brass, which means exactly one thing: the agent is working. The empty state is the pawn from the app icon, at the size of a paragraph. - **A status light.** One small lamp in the pane's header, breathing while the agent works, red if a turn failed. A glance answers "is it doing anything" without reading a line of text. - **The agent's own door.** A pawn in the tab strip, brass while the pane is open. It was reachable only by a keyboard shortcut before.
## Past chats
- **Conversations are kept.** "New chat" used to throw the last one away — the transcript and the model's memory of it both. Every chat is now archived as you work, listed newest first, and reopening one continues it rather than merely replaying it. - Delete is there, and asks once.
## OpenRouter, properly
- **A searchable model picker.** The old control offered three tiers, which is the right question for a router that resolves "sonnet" and the wrong one for a gateway with 450 models. The picker lists what your key can actually use, with price per million tokens on every row. - **Only models that can call tools are offered.** A model that cannot click can only talk about the page, so offering it would be offering a broken agent. 316 of 381 catalogue entries qualify. - **Model ids survive.** OpenRouter names models `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`; the app used to fold that to `sonnet`, which is a 404. Names are now sent exactly as set. - **The address is no longer doubled.** `…/api/v1` used to become `…/api/v1/v1/chat/completions`.
## Passwords and passkeys
- **Touch ID before a secret.** Picking an account read the keychain and typed the password with no check that the person asking was the person who saved it. It now asks first. A name-only screen asks for nothing, because there is no secret on it yet. - **Two-step sign-ins fill.** On a page that asks for the name and then the password — Google, most Microsoft sign-ins, anything on Okta — choosing an account used to say "couldn't find the sign-in fields". It fills the name and tells you the password follows. - **Passkeys use the ones you already have.** The browser entitlement is now honoured, so signing in offers the passkeys from iCloud Keychain — the same ones Safari and your iPhone hold — rather than a separate store. - **Bluetooth.** The usage description the system needs for cross-device passkeys is now declared, so the hand-off to your phone no longer crashes.
## Updates
- **Sparkle 2, on Gambit's own feed.** Releases are EdDSA-signed and verified against a public key in the app, install on quit rather than swapping a running bundle, and download as deltas.
## Under the hood
- The bundle is named Gambit, its log subsystems and message handlers say so, and the addon bridge shim matches what the Swift side calls.
